coverage.terminals_cross_check: Ran the sibling repo's scripts/fsru_sync_check.py, read-only, from lng-terminals-researcher/scripts/ as cwd (its --gem-csv default only resolves from that directory). Two bugs in that read-only script were worked around, not fixed, per the 'read-only repo -> report, don't touch' rule: (1) load_carrier_vessels() in fsru_sync_check.py only recognizes CSV headers 'VesselName'/'Vessel Name'/'vessel_name', so it silently read zero records against our backend's actual 'Name' header -- worked around by writing a translated copy of the backend (VesselName/IMO/Status/Owner/Operator/VesselType columns) to my scratchpad and pointing --carrier-export at that, without editing the sibling script. (2) gather_gem_fsrus() in the same script does not filter on facility_type, so its raw output mixes true import-side FSRUs with export-side FLNG/liquefaction units; I filtered GEM's own gem_export.csv to facility_type == 'import' myself (255 rows) and built an independent name-matching pass (using this repo's normalize_vessel_name plus multi-name splitting and substring containment) rather than trusting the sibling script's bucket assignments. Both issues should be reported to whoever owns lng-terminals-researcher for a real fix -- I did not, and will not, edit that repo. The GEM-side data itself (gem_export.csv) is a static snapshot dated 2026-09-10, 13 days stale relative to this pass; any floating unit GEM has added, renamed, or reclassified since then would not appear here. Of the 255 import-facility floating units, 161 carry no assigned vessel name yet in GEM's own data (early-stage proposals) and were not meaningfully checkable; 88 matched an existing backend row (84 by the direct name/substring match, plus 4 more resolved by hand in this pass -- Excelerate Acadia, Solidarity, Turquoise P, SC Serenity); the remaining 6 real-named units are each classified above as scope question or out of scope. None of the 255 produced a genuine new discovery candidate not already covered by an existing backend row or by this stream's own GIIGNL small-scale findings.
